thread:
maya: Quick question — for correlation, do we prefer services to inject the trace id into logs at the source or rely on the OTEL collector to enrich logs at ingest? seeing gaps in dashboards.
ben: I'd vote for source injection. collectors can miss spans (sampling / timing), and enrichment becomes a best-effort. if the app writes it, correlation is deterministic.
sophia: Agree with ben but nuance: many of our older services log as plain text. We need a small library/middleware to add trace context to structured logs first. Otherwise we'll just be stuffing trace ids into unstructured blobs.
jamie: Also cost/retention question — adding trace_id field expands indexed docs in ES. Are we sure that's okay for high-volume services? we should consider making the field non-indexed or keep as keyword with low-cardinality settings.
ben: Good point. We Can standardize on a single field name and mapping. Proposal: "telemetry.trace_id" as a keyword, doc_values=false for huge streams, or store as a runtime field for ad-hoc correlation.
maya: runtime fields sound nice but slow for alerting. For dashboards we probably want direct field for fast joins. Maybe only index on a sample or for requests route logs.
sophia: Implementation sketch for app-side injection (python example):
```python
from opentelemetry import trace

def inject_trace_id(record):
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    if span is None:
        return
    trace_id = span.get_span_context().trace_id
    record["telemetry.trace_id"] = format(trace_id, '032x')
```
This runs in logger adapter/middleware so only structured logs get the field.
ben: For go services we'd do similar in a zap/zapcore hook. can add helpers in our internal libs (redwood/logs).
otel-bot: :robot_face: telemetry: observed ~12% of logs in prod missing trace context last 24h (svc=ingest, svc=webhooks). See https://console.redwood.internal/d/telemetry/correlate?from=24h
jamie: Another concern: privacy/PII scanning in logs. trace ids themselves are fine, but we must ensure no other span attributes leak into logs accidentally when serializing context. guardrails needed.
maya: Agreed. Add linter + test to logging lib to prevent accidental span.attributes dump.
sophia: Collector enrichment is still useful for non-instrumented services (3rd-party adapters, legacy workers). We should keep an OTEL processor that tries to attach trace.id when available, but treat it as secondary.
ben: We should also document sampling interactions: if traces are sampled out early, enrichment won't find a span. So app-level write wins.
jamie: Ops: we need mapping guidance per index template + a cost estimate. I'll run a rough calc for top 10 producers and show size delta if telemetry.trace_id is indexed vs not.
maya: Next steps: 1) agree field name (telemetry.trace_id) 2) PR for logging lib (js/py/go) to inject when span present 3) collector enrichment as fallback 4) index mapping guidance + cost runbook 5) add CI lints to prevent accidental attribute dumps.
ben: +1 from infra. I'll draft a tiny RFC and an example PR for python.
sophia: I'll add examples for zap and bunyan in the repo.
jamie: I'll post the cost numbers by EOD tomorrow.
